cmd.analyze.long.other: Analyze binlog files. Pass - to read one binary binlog from a pipe; stdin is copied to a temporary file because parsing needs seek. Default text, JSON, markdown, and HTML rank Top Threads by rows, events, bytes, or transactions and show thread_id plus user@host and schema when the binlog has them. They also list Hot Rows: the primary keys touched by the most UPDATE and DELETE row images, when binlog_row_metadata=FULL names the key. Default text and JSON name, per transaction, server_id, thread_id, GTID, and xid or XA xid when the events have them. user@host is shown only when the binlog has it. A field the binlog does not have stays absent.

cmd.flashback.long.other: Print SQL that reverses selected ROW changes: DELETE becomes INSERT of the before-image, INSERT becomes DELETE, and UPDATE returns the row to its before-image. Statements are in reverse binlog order, one transaction at a time. Select rows with the same table, schema, --dml, time, position, and GTID filters as analyze. The script goes to stdout. Review it before applying. This command does not connect to a database. --schema-file names generated columns when the binlog has no CREATE TABLE, and must describe the table as it was at incident time. ENUM is the member index and SET is the bitmask. ENUM index 0 is restored by dropping strict sql_mode for that statement only. An expression binlogviz cannot evaluate is refused unless --allow-unverified-generated is set. A logged value that contradicts the expression is refused either way.
